parent: Boots UK (provider: Boots Digital Health Ltd, CQC registered; runs on the Lemonaid Health UK platform)
model: High-street pharmacy's online doctor: a men-only questionnaire for licensed finasteride or Propecia tablets (optionally bundled with Regaine foam), reviewed by a clinician, sold as one-off packs with store pick-up or free delivery.

access.accountWall: After the health questions. Nothing asks for an email before that: after postcode, birth gender and date of birth the site itself creates a placeholder "temporary user" (POST users/temp). The first screen we could not pass is the ID photo step at /camera/id ("Let's confirm it's you": a selfie and a photo of your ID), which comes straight after the last health question. Account set-up (email, name, phone, address, password) is the next task after the photos, then delivery and payment. No recommendation is shown before the wall: the patient has already picked the medicine.
blockers: ID photos (selfie + photo ID) are required before account set-up; photos are outside the research rules, so nothing after the health questions was seen.
curl to the marketing site was blocked by the Imperva/Incapsula bot protection after about five quick requests; the normal browser (walk.js) was not blocked. Nothing was done to get round it.
access.coverageNote: Walked live with the baseline man from the entry page to the ID photo screen for the first-time, tablets-only route (all 19 question screens). The three other routes (first-time bundle, returning tablets, returning bundle) were walked to their first health question, which made the site serve their full question sets; those questions are recorded from the served definitions, not clicked through. All four definitions are saved. No account, email, name, phone, address, password, photo or payment was entered. A postcode had to be typed to start: the placeholder postcode found in the site's own code (N1 0QH) was used; it is a location check, not a contact detail. There is no women's hair-loss consultation to walk. Stage 2: 14 live one-change runs (x00 to x13, runs/x*) confirmed the gates, the product list limits and that no answer changes the product, price or flow on screen. Stage 3 (independent check): 14 more live runs (runs/verify-*) replayed all four baselines, the gates (plus age 18 and Guernsey), the out-of-stock tile, completed the bundle age-50 run, walked the returning bundle route end to end for the first time, tested one amber and one red answer on their own and the Propecia bundle. It found that the order JSON does record a triage label (answer_status), which stage 2 had missed.

engineSummary: There is no recommending engine on screen; the website is a gate, a price list and a fixed form. Three hard stops come first and were all seen live: postcode (Jersey and Guernsey refused), birth sex (female refused) and age (under 18 refused; 18 and 75 accepted with no change). The man then says first-time or returning (no proof) and picks medicine, brand and pack himself. First-timers can only pick one-month packs (bigger packs are marked out of stock in the served product list and cannot be clicked); "returning" unlocks all packs. Tablets or bundle, first-time or returning, picks one of four fixed questionnaires; Propecia uses the same one as generic. Follow-ups appear one level deep. Every option carries a plain/amber/red status. The screen ignores it: even nine stacked red flags and three "I will stop my consultation" answers reach the same ID photo screen with the same product and price. But the server does use it: once the answers are posted, the order is labelled "Normal", "Query", "Warning" or "Danger" for the clinician. Asking to drop Regaine does not change the order. All decisions are left to a clinician after ID photos, account and payment.
strengths: Trusted pharmacy brand, CQC-registered provider, named clinical lead, pick-up in any Boots store within about 2 business hours of approval.
Licensed medicines only; clear safety wording (pregnancy, PSA tests, depression and sexual side effects) repeated as must-acknowledge screens.
No email needed until after the questions; pay only if approved; no subscription lock-in.
Bundle questionnaire handles Regaine limits (age 49 licence limit, blood pressure, scalp skin).
Every gate it does have is immediate and plainly worded (sex, age, postcode), with signposting to a GP or Boots Health Hub.
Safety follow-ups appear exactly when relevant (pregnancy, suicidal thoughts, blood pressure with Regaine, off-label Regaine over 49), so the clinician gets context in the patient's own answers.
weaknesses: Men only; nothing for women's hair loss.
Very narrow range: finasteride 1 mg tablets with or without Regaine foam. No topical finasteride, oral minoxidil, dutasteride, compounded sprays, shampoos or supplements.
The patient must choose medicine and pack before answering anything; no guidance or recommendation.
No photos of the scalp are asked for; pattern is one four-option question with wording errors ("Tick all that apply" on a single-choice question).
Red-flag answers do not stop the flow on screen; the patient can go on to ID photos and payment details and only then be refused.
First-time list showed most packs as "Out of stock"; ID photo step adds friction; dated copy (pages last reviewed 2021 and 2023, placeholder text left in the content data).

Live tests show the screen never acts on its own red flags: patients who say they will stop, who have patchy or complete hair loss, or suicidal thoughts still reach ID photos, account and payment steps. The server only labels the order ("Danger") for later review.
Choosing "tablets alone" in the bundle form does not change the basket; the patient still sees the bundle price.
"Returning" is self-declared with no check, and it unlocks bigger packs that first-timers cannot buy.

No questions about goals, how much hair loss bothers the patient, preferences (tablet vs topical) or previous non-finasteride treatments; nothing about women, so half of hair-loss patients are turned away.
opportunities: A guided recommendation (pattern, goals, preferences) instead of a price list.
Options for men who cannot or will not take oral finasteride, and a women's pathway.
Immediate, kind on-screen outcomes for red-flag answers with signposting, instead of late refusal.
Scalp photo review and progress tracking; subscription convenience with easy pause.
Act on red flags at once with a clear "this is not right for you, here is what to do" screen, saving the patient ID photos and sign-up.
Let the questionnaire change the basket live (e.g. drop Regaine for blood-pressure patients, suggest topical options for men who do not want oral finasteride).
Offer longer first supplies or a subscription after a proper first review, instead of stock flags.
Serve women and the "no finasteride" group (topical finasteride, oral or topical minoxidil, combination sprays), which Boots does not sell online.

verification.verdict: The core picture holds up: Boots Online Doctor has no on-screen recommending engine, men only, three entry gates (sex, age 18+, mainland UK postcode), the patient picks the product, and that pick chooses one of four fixed questionnaires that are saved word for word. Prices and products were all re-checked live and match. One important claim was wrong: answers are not ignored. The server labels each order Normal, Query, Warning or Danger from the option statuses, which is how red flags reach the clinician. With that corrected, the report can be trusted as labelled for everything before the ID photo wall; nothing after the wall (clinician decisions, refusals, switches) is known.
